### Data

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyquant)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# unemp_raw <- tq_get(
#   c("UNRATE", "ORUR", "CAUR", "TXUR", "NYUR"),
#   get  = "economic.data",
#   from = "1976-01-01"
# )
# head(unemp_raw)
# 
# dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
# write_rds(unemp_raw, "data/unemp_raw.rds")

unemp_raw= read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")
```

The data set includes the monthly unemployment rates reported by FRED of the United States, California, New York, Oregon, and Texas starting from January of 1976 to September of 2026.

### Wrangling

```{r}
#Cleaning Data
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region= case_when(
      symbol== "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol== "ORUR" ~ "Oregon",
      symbol== "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol== "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol== "NYUR" ~ "New York")
  )

#Wrangle Data 
unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region,date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate= replace(
      unemployment_rate, date== as.Date("2025-10-01"),
      unemployment_rate[date== as.Date("2025-09-01")]
    )
  ) |>
ungroup()

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region,date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change= unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate))|>
  ungroup()

unemp_recent <- unemp |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2015-01-01"))

#Summary
unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate =mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm= TRUE),
    min_rate =min(unemployment_rate, na.rm= TRUE),
    max_rate =max(unemployment_rate, na.rm= TRUE))
unemp_summary |>
  kable(
    digits= 2,
    col.names= c("Region", "Mean Rate", "Min Rate", "Max Rate"),
    caption= "Unemployment Rate Summary Stats"
  )
#Summary Recent
unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate =mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm= TRUE),
    min_rate =min(unemployment_rate, na.rm= TRUE),
    max_rate =max(unemployment_rate, na.rm= TRUE))
unemp_recent_summary |>
kable(
  digits= 2,
  col.names= c("Region", "Mean Rate", "Min Rate", "Max Rate"),
  caption= "Recent Unemployment Rate Summary Stats"
)

#Extremes
unemp_top_increases <- unemp |>
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n=5)

unemp_top_decreases <- unemp |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n=5)

#Omit 2020
unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- unemp|>
  filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01")| date > as.Date("2020-12-31")) |>
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n=5)
unemp_top_increases_no_covid |>
kable(
  digits= 2,
  col.names= c("State Symbol", "Date", "Rate", "Region", "Change in Rate"),
  caption= "Greatest month to month decreases in the unemployment rate excluding 2020"
)

unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- unemp|>
  filter(date < as.Date("2020-01-01")| date > as.Date("2020-12-31")) |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n=5) 
unemp_top_decreases_no_covid |>
  kable(
    digits= 2,
    col.names= c("State Symbol", "Date", "Rate", "Region", "Change in Rate"),
    caption= "Greatest month to month ncreases in the unemployment rate excluding 2020"
  )
```

### Visualization

```{r}
#Visualize Data
ggplot( 
  data= unemp,
  mapping= aes(x=date, y=unemployment_rate, color=region)
) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title="Unemployment Rate by Region",
    x="Date",
    y="Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color="Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot( 
  data= unemp,
  mapping= aes(x=date, y=unemployment_rate, color=region)
) +
  geom_line() +
facet_wrap(~region, ncol=2, axes = "all_x") +
  labs(
    title="Unemployment Rate by Region",
    x="Date",
    y="Unemployment Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot( 
  data= unemp_summary,
  mapping= aes(fct_reorder(region,mean_rate), y=mean_rate)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title="Mean Unemployment Rate by Region",
    x="Region",
    y="Mean Unemployment Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot( 
  data= unemp_recent,
  mapping= aes(x=date, y=unemployment_rate, color=region)
) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~region, axes= "all_x") +
  labs(
    title="Unemployment Rate by Region",
    x="Date",
    y="Unemployment Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
I plotted the recent unemployment rate by region to see the effects of the
COVID-19 pandemic on unemployment rates. The plot shows a significant spike in unemployment rates around the year 2020 with a decrease in the following years.


### Reflection

This problem set helped me re-familiarize myself with R syntax, especially with the tidyverse functions and their inputs. I had some trouble figuring out the arguments to each function and general syntax errors (such as forgetting commas or including the wrong symbol in an function), however I found that I was comfortable with the workflow and understood generally what functions and code I needed to get the desired result. I've also gotten more comfortable with making commits to github and navigating through github in general.
